# Same setup as merge_access_changed_defers_seal_workflow, but replayed with a
# rebase. The deferred seal is done by the pre-commit hook, and `git rebase
# --continue` runs no hook at all - so the advice must point at `sesam seal`
# instead of promising it happens on commit.

sesam-repo admin base.txt ours.txt theirs.txt

exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec sesam tell --user carol --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY --group ops
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s'

exec git checkout -b topic
exec sesam add s --group-add dev
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: dev only'

exec git checkout master
exec sesam add s --group-add ops
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'master: ops only'

# Replay topic onto master. The content merges, the recipients disagree, so the
# seal is deferred - and nothing downstream would pick it up, so the driver
# reports a conflict instead of letting git commit the pre-merge object.
exec git checkout topic
! exec git rebase master
stderr 'access to it changed on both sides'
stderr 'sesam seal'
stderr 'git rebase --continue'
! stderr 'sealed with the merged recipients when you commit'

# The merged plaintext is on disk, so the advice works: seal it, stage it, go on.
grep 'first = OURS' s
grep 'last = THEIRS' s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git -c core.editor=true rebase --continue

# Both sides made it into the committed object, and both recipient sets stuck.
exec sesam verify
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'OURS'
stdout 'THEIRS'

-- base.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = BASE
-- ours.txt --
first = OURS
middle = BASE
last = BASE
-- theirs.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = THEIRS
